A.question: On abrupt process termination before JSONL newline, can private audit detect torn capture ledger and refuse success rather than silently treating it as reviewed?
A.estimand: Negative safety test under SIGKILL on disposable synthetic manifest
A.acceptance: Spawn child writes deliberately incomplete synthetic JSONL record and fsyncs; SIGKILL only child; afterward private audit raises INCOMPLETE_LEDGER_RECORD and CLI code2; no raw identifiers exposed.

rivals: Filesystem contains no record, so no parser evidence (process stopped before write)
A persistent but unterminated line is detected and fails closed
Torn partial line could parse as complete valid JSON if newline ignored (regression C20 addressed newline)

C: Execute isolated process-termination fixture in container and commit a POSIX-only test invoking existing read-only audit path. Distinguish actual process-kill test from power outage and full transaction recovery.

D.falsifier: Process interrupted after flushed fragment but audit reports normal success or creates files during read.
D.safety: Only disposable tmp_path, fake data, local process, no HTTP/private originals or CI.
